source.title: Explicitly Bayesian Regularizations in Deep Learning

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation.
record.tranche_reason: Tests width and random-label generalization on a synthetic dataset and measures a proposed prior-distribution quantity, using a method different from the cited original studies.
record.gate_note: The paper's discussion of other architecture, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, and sharpness results cites prior work; those are not its own results. Its own experiments measure synthetic-data test error as channel count changes and random-label test error. The random-label experiment's text is internally inconsistent: it describes zero training error and very high test error, then says the model has good random-label generalization.
record.test_reason: The study tests V1 in a new synthetic digit setting: CNN3 generalizes on digit labels yet fits random training labels with approximately chance-level test accuracy. Its width comparison does not establish performance beyond the width required for zero training error, so it does not test V2's defining condition.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they interpret early hidden layers as Bayesian priors providing explicit regularization, explain the width result through improved prior modeling, and attribute chance-level random-label classification to the learned likelihood. Their statement about good random-label generalization refers specifically to accurate input-distribution modeling, rather than good classification accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: Synthetic-data experiments on three CNNs, varying first-layer channel count and evaluating one random-label case; does not reproduce the original datasets or model/recipe suite.
record.method_sensitivity: First convolutional layer channel count is varied; the text reports lower test error with more channels. Random-label outcome is reported for CNN3.

fits_no_version.finding: Across first-layer channel counts of 4, 12 and 20, the authors report decreasing test error over 30 epochs, without establishing a post-interpolation comparison.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing first-layer width can improve test accuracy in these synthetic-digit CNNs under a fixed 30-epoch budget.

record.problems: Synthetic dataset is custom-generated and the results are presented without numeric test-error values in Figure 3. Random-label reporting is internally contradictory: the paper states very high testing error around 90%, then says CNN3 has good generalization on random labels. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible own-result rows identified. Section 4.2's KL divergence values concern the proposed prior-distribution validation, not a measure named by the claim versions; it is not mapped to a version row.

untested.parts: The named benchmark datasets and architectures; confirmation that training recipes are identical across label conditions and omit explicit regularization.
Whether widening beyond an established zero-training-error threshold continues lowering test error under training to convergence; no interpolation threshold or double-descent peak is established.
Convolutional versus fully connected classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD performance under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects and recipe adaptations under controlled epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Accuracy after removing memorized versus randomly selected training examples.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. The random-label outcome supports V1 rather than limiting its scope. No precise Figure 3 values or uncertainty estimates can be recovered from the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Tests one CNN on one synthetic dataset with random labels; does not test the named architectures, natural labels, or same recipes on CIFAR-10 or ImageNet.

Tests three CNNs differing in the first convolutional layer's channel count on the synthetic dataset; does not test one-hidden-layer ReLU networks, MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10, or a sweep explicitly extending beyond an identified zero-training-error threshold.

rows.check: Zero training error and approximately 90% test error support V1's random-label arm. Figure 5's legend names CNN1, whereas its caption and Section 4.4 identify CNN3; retain CNN3 with this discrepancy flagged. The reference to good generalization concerns the estimated input distribution, not random-label classification accuracy.

relationships.condition: CNN3 on synthetic NIST-derived digit images with digit labels versus random labels
relationships.reason: R3 reports digit-label test performance far above chance; R4 reports zero random-label training error and approximately 90% test error, consistent with chance accuracy on ten classes.
relationships.display_finding: The reported digit-label generalization, zero random-label training error and approximately chance random-label test performance remain unverified from the available source.
